paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Multiple studies of the cognitive processes underlying memory consolidation (permanent memories) have required the treatment and retraining of animal and human subjects to complete an early task. These have vastly contributed to our knowledge.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Bernard Agranoff’s ground-breaking work with goldfish showed that administering protein synthesis inhibitors caused the fish to forget what they had previously learned. Moreover, he administered the blockers of protein synthesis immediately, before teaching the fish. Surprisingly, the protein inhibitors hindered long-term memory yet had no effect on short-term memory: the fish learned the task normally but quickly forgot it.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), which inhibits long-term memory, preserves short-term memory, according to mounting evidence. Ivan Izquierdo discovered that certain pharmacological treatments can impair short-term memory without affecting memory development. On the flip side, a theory was put forth that long-term memory and short-term memory are not dependent on one another. This was suggested by Canadian psychologist Donald Hebb in 1949.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: These results demonstrate that our experiences generate simultaneous and potentially separate periods of memory, each with its own lifespan. The reason for this is unknown, but all of these clinical and experimental results strongly show that the brain makes recent and remote memories differently.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: To adapt to an environment that is always changing, we need a memory that can be generated quickly. The majority of contemporary building codes, for example, stipulate that stair step heights must be the same. After ascending or descending a few steps, we immediately remember their heights and think that the rest will be the same. If they do not correspond, we may trip and fall. It would be of little use if we could only recall the step heights after several hours have passed and the memory has solidified.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The majority of this theory’s support comes from clinical and experimental data that medications and illnesses affecting brain function can have an effect on long-term memory development. Many other sorts of evidence show that after learning, memories gradually solidify over time. Human participants trained in a visual skill showed no improvement until eight hours after the training was complete, and then showed even greater improvement the following day, as reported by Avi Karni and Dov Sagi. Also, the mastery was maintained over a long period of time.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: In addition, studies employing human brain scans to carefully assess neuronal activity induced by learning have revealed that these changes linger for hours after learning. Reza Shadmehr and Henry Holcomb performed innovative research using brain imaging to assess brain activity in various regions of the brain shortly after training human volunteers in a motor learning task including arm and hand movements. Although the subjects’ performance remained consistent for several hours following training, their brain function did not; various regions of the brain were extremely active at various times over the several hours of training. The activity changed from the prefrontal cortex to the recognized movement-regulating motor cortex and cerebellar cortex. Integration of the motor ability appeared to include activation of many neural networks, which maintained underlying brain processes.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: In addition, there is evidence that learning-induced associations in the firing of neurons in the cerebral cortex persist for days following training. In a series of extensive experiments with rats implanted with diodes in the auditory cortex, Norman Weinberger found that after a narrow band tone was recurrently paired with footshock, nerve cells in the auditory cortex reacted more firmly to the particular tone and less strongly to other tones with various frequencies. Interestingly, the uniqueness of the neurons’ responses to the particular tone used in learning remained higher for a number of days after training had concluded.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Why our long-term memories grow slowly is not easily explicable. It is definitely puzzling why we have a type of memory on which we must rely for many hours, days, or even a lifetime, yet which is so sensitive to disturbance quickly after its formation. The brain circuitry that centralizes long-term memory over time may have been an evolutionary afterthought. In addition, the size and complexity of our mammalian brains may result in slower memory integration. These beliefs are simple to debunk. Every known animal species possesses both short- and long-term memory and is subject to forgetfulness. Birds, bees, mollusks, fish, and rodents have long-term memory, similar to humans. Memory consolidation has existed and been conserved since the beginning of evolution.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Even though there appears to be no compelling reason to believe that a biological system such as the brain could not rapidly develop a long-lasting memory, this is not the case. Memory consolidation must therefore fulfill a crucial adaptive purpose or function. There is strong evidence that slow consolidation is adaptive, as it allows neurobiological mechanisms to adjust the memory intensity for experiences immediately after learning. Intriguingly, a substantial body of evidence indicates that therapies taken quickly after training may both improve and damage memory.

passages.title: Taking Us Back to Paradise City

paragraphs.text: The hard rock band Guns N’ Roses was founded in 1985 by Axl Rose and Tracii Guns and took its name from its two founding members, who served as the group’s main guitarists at the time. Few could have anticipated the band’s level of popularity at the time. The band, which became a symbol of the hedonistic rebelliousness of the 1980s and 1990s punk-rock era, has, after much rumor, resurrected itself for another assault on the music charts. The band has sold more than 100 million albums worldwide, including 46 million in the United States alone, to date. A new world tour has officially started for GNR, as the group is now known. And as it begins a new chapter of its journey, we look back at the band’s colorful and frequently contentious past.

In the beginning, the band lineup saw a lot of changes. Tracii Guns, a founding member, was replaced as the lead guitarist by Slash since he missed the rehearsals. Slash also added his close friend Steven Adler to the lineup after the band’s former drummer Rob Gardner left for personal reasons. Axl Rose (vocals), Izzy Stradlin (rhythm guitar), Duff McKagan (bass), Slash (lead guitar), and Steven Adler (drums) entered their first tour, known as the “Hell Tour,” after settling into their positions and completing the line-up. The band found its chemistry while touring, and even though it was only able to put out one four-track EP, Like a Suicide, during this time, the foundation for future success was laid. This was because the group quickly developed a reputation for giving energetic live performances.

The group’s debut album, Appetite for Destruction, was released on July 21st, 1987. The album remained at the bottom of the charts for over a year before the band’s representative was able to persuade MTV execs to play Welcome to the Jungle, the album’s lead single, during their afternoon rotations. However, success wasn’t by any means instantaneous. Rock and punk fans soon noticed and started clamoring for the video in droves. The album’s second US hit, “Sweet Child of Mine,” the song and its accompanying music video received regular airplay and quickly rose to the top of the US charts, in large part due to strong grassroots support. After receiving invites to participate at significant international rock festivals, a world tour began. The band was currently well on its way to becoming famous and wealthy.

All of the band members led extreme lives, but drummer Adler’s lifestyle ultimately got the best of him. He could no longer perform with the band due to the severity of his drug use and was sacked in July 1990. Matt Sorum took his place. The group also gained a sixth member when Dizzy Reed joined as the group’s keyboardist. The band then began working on its most ambitious project to date, releasing two albums, Use Your Illusion 1 and Use Your Illusion 2, at the same time. The risk paid off brilliantly as the albums shot to numbers one and two in the charts, the first time a band had ever accomplished such a feat. However, despite being on top of a wave, the band members were constantly dogged by controversy, especially singer Rose, who was among other things charged with assault and accused of inciting a riot that claimed many lives. Nevertheless, the Use Your Illusion Tour ended with a bang, drawing record crowds and lasting an amazing 28 months.

But just when it seemed like the band could not fail, everything started to slowly fall apart. Prior to Slash’s official departure in 1996, the band took a break during which time they did not record or tour. Rose and Slash both experienced personal problems. Rose replaced most of the other band members who left after Slash did, but it took a full nine years until a highly anticipated reunion performance was given in Las Vegas. The band’s anticipated new album, Chinese Democracy, never appeared, and tour plans were frequently postponed or scrapped entirely. Chinese Democracy wasn’t actually released until 2008 when Rose was the last survivor of the original band.

Following the release of Chinese Democracy, the band embarked on a new global tour, which got generally favorable reviews but was marred by controversy due to Rose’s penchant for being late for shows and his stage presence, both of which have drawn much ire. After all is said and done, though, GNR’s ongoing appeal cannot be disputed. Just as they did before when the band first became popular, devoted fans continue to queue up in the thousands to get tickets for every new tour stop. The only difference is that they are more anticipating than hoping for a fantastic performance today, but that’s rock and roll, baby!

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Although the game itself is much older, football as we know it now originated in Britain in the nineteenth century. In fact, the term “football” has historically referred to games performed on foot, as opposed to those played on horseback, so kicking a ball was not always a component. It has generally been played by men, although at the end of the 17th century, married and unmarried women in a Scottish town played the game. The married women consistently won.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Tsu’chu, which was played in China, was the earliest form of football for which we have evidence, and may date back 3,000 years. It was performed in front of the Emperor during his birthday celebrations. It entailed kicking a leather ball through a 30-40 cm aperture into a small net attached to long bamboo canes, a feat that required exceptional ability and precision.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The Japanese ‘kemari’, which dates back to roughly the fifth century and is still played today, is a variant of the game that also originated in the Far East. This is a form of circular football, a more dignified and ceremonial event requiring specific skills, but not competitive in the same way that the Chinese game was, nor is there any hint of fight for possession of the ball. The players had to transfer the ball to one another in a somewhat confined area without allowing it to hit the ground.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The Romans had a far more exciting game called ‘harpastum’. Each team member had a distinct tactical assignment and exhibited a loud interest in the game’s progress and score. The involvement of the feet was so tiny as to be negligible. The game remained popular for 700 or 800 years, but despite its introduction to England, it is unlikely to be considered a precursor to modern football.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The game that flourished in Britain between the 8th and 19th centuries was significantly different from all previously known versions; it was more disorganised, aggressive, spontaneous, and typically played by an undetermined number of players. Frequently, the games consisted of a fierce competition between entire communities. Kicking opponents was permitted, as was virtually anything else.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Even though the authorities intervened often to limit football as a public nuisance, there was a great deal of passion for the sport. During the 14th and 15th centuries, football was ruled illegal in England, Scotland, and France due to the unrest that sometimes accompanied it or because it prevented subjects from practising more useful military disciplines. None of these initiatives had an appreciable effect.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The popularity of the somewhat more organised Italian game ‘Calcio’ had a significant impact on the development of football in England throughout the sixteenth century. Richard Mulcaster, a school headmaster, was a notable fan of English football, which remained as harsh as ever. He emphasised that it had educational value and fostered health and vitality. Mulcaster stated that all that was required was a little refinement, a cap on the number of players per team, and most crucially, a referee to monitor the game.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Until the early 19th century, when a number of influential English schools created their own modifications, the game existed in a disorganised state. In some schools, particularly Rugby School, the ball could be carried or touched with the hands, and opponents could be tripped and kicked. In educational circles, it was acknowledged that football, as a team sport, helped to foster values such as loyalty, altruism, cooperation, subordination, and respect for team spirit. In schools, a ‘games cult’ arose, and football became a required part of the curriculum.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: In 1863, the culmination of events was reached. At Cambridge University, there was a movement to develop consistent standards and rules that would be accepted by everybody, but there were essentially two camps: Rugby School and others intended to continue with their own version of the game, which included permitting players to carry the ball. Eleven London clubs and schools dispatched delegations in October of the same year to draw up a set of fundamental regulations to regulate their matches. This gathering signified the establishment of the Football Association.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: The issue over kicking and tripping opponents and carrying the ball was exhaustively examined at this and following sessions until, on December 8, the most ardent proponents of the Rugby style departed, resulting in a definitive split between rugby and football. Within eight years, the Football Association had 50 member clubs and launched the FA Cup, the first football competition in the globe.
